title: Trace compactification and query indexes for cost-efficient analytics observability
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: Our analytics ingest pipeline produces high-cardinality trace payloads for console/analytics flows. Storing raw spans and full event payloads is driving long-term storage and query costs; investigators are also seeing slow P95 query latency on ad-hoc SLO postmortems.

Goal: Reduce trace storage footprint and query cost by ~40% while preserving fidelity for SLO investigations and post-incident replay. Provide efficient index paths for the common investigative queries (time window + tenant + route/component + error flag), and add a hot/warm/cold trace tiering strategy with transparent retrieval.

Success criteria (measurable):
- End-to-end storage cost for analytics traces reduced by >= 35% in the warm tier (baseline: Nov 2025).
- P95 trace query latency for SLO investigations reduced from ~1.4s to <= 700ms for hot/warm queries.
- No increase in missed SLI alert investigations due to missing trace fidelity (sampling-adjusted).
- Rollout feature flag that allows rollback without data loss.

Constraints and non-goals:
- We will not change primary SLI definitions in this ticket.
- This is an observability-cost optimization; not a full redesign of trace format for all services.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Trace compactification pipeline (ingest-time):
   - Fingerprint repeated fields and large event payloads using a content-addressed key (SHA256 short) and store the blob once in a dedup store. In trace documents keep a small reference and a compact delta when needed.
   - Coalesce contiguous KV cache/serving-runtime spans that have identical metadata into a single span with count/length metadata.
   - Delta-encode timestamp arrays and token offsets for long traces to reduce redundancy.

2) Cost-efficient query indexes:
   - Introduce composite inverted index: (tenant_id,date_bucket,route_tag,error_flag) optimized for the common investigator queries.
   - Maintain a light-weight secondary index for quick existence checks (used by console UI to decide if full retrieval is required).

3) Storage tiering:
   - Hot tier: full expanded traces for last 7 days; stored in fast index with full payload.
   - Warm tier: compactified traces and dedup blobs for 7-90 days.
   - Cold tier: metadata-only traces for 90+ days (retain just enough to reconstruct a minimal postmortem when requested).
   - Provide an on-demand expansion path (background job) to rehydrate compacted traces if an investigator requests full fidelity; track rehydrate request cost.

4) Query path and API changes:
   - New trace retrieval API parameter compact=false|true to control auto-expansion (default true).
   - Augment console investigation flow to use index checks before fetching full traces; show an estimated rehydrate cost and allow user confirmation.

Metrics to track (telemetry):
- Storage bytes/month by tier (hot/warm/cold), and per-tenant breakdown for top 10 tenants.
- Trace ingest CPU/latency delta due to compactification.
- P95/P99 query latency for composite-index lookups and full retrievals.
- Rehydrate requests per day and associated cost.
- Fraction of SLO investigations requiring rehydration vs resolved from compacted traces.

Rollout plan and experiments:
- Phase 0 (poC): Implement compactification transform in a sidecar processor and run for 10% of traffic (internal tenants) with feature flag. Collect query latency and rehydrate events.
- Phase 1 (pilot): Enable warm-tier storage for non-critical tenants (30% traffic); validate cost and investigator UX.
- Phase 2 (gradual ramp): 70% traffic; add UI prompt and dashboards; iterate on index tuning.
- Phase 3 (GA): Default warm-tier retention policy and full index; document costs and admin controls.

Fallbacks and rollback:
- All compactification is reversible; dedup blobs kept for at least 7 days after toggle off.
- Feature flag toggles route all newly-ingested traces to legacy full-storage path.

Open questions and trade-offs: 
- Dedup blob GC window: shorter window reduces storage but risks losing ability to rehydrate older compacted traces. Recommended initial policy: 30 days GC for non-critical tenants.
- Index write amplification: composite indexes add write cost; need to balance index granularity vs query benefits.
- GDPR/PII: deduped payloads may contain PII; ensure KMS encryption and per-tenant keying for blobs as required by Private deployments.

Next steps / concrete tasks:
- ENG: Prototype compactification transform and local benchmark (task 1).
- ENG: Implement composite index schema and benchmark query latency (task 2).
- ENG/Console PM: Wire a console prompt and cost-estimate modal for rehydrates (task 3).
- SRE: Define DOCS and runbooks for rehydrate cost spikes and GC incidents (task 4).

Artifacts and links: see attachments for design notes and dashboards.
